injuryReports.name: Jayden Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams could miss consecutive games due to a knee injury, which would mark the second missed game of his young career. If the seventh-round rookie must miss another contest, Josh Fryar would be set to start Sunday's game at left tackle.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Zachary Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter will remain on IR for Week 10 and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Rams. The defensive tackle logged three consecutive limited practices after being designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: Gaines was set to start at center due to the absence of Hjalte Froholdt (concussion). With Gaines also unable to suit up due to an ankle injury, Hayden Conner will make his first career start at center against Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Hjalte Froholdt
injuryReports.returnComment: Froholdt appeared on the Cardinals' injury report Wednesday with a concussion and has not progressed in his recovery. Both Froholdt and backup center Jon Gaines (ankle) will not suit up for Sunday's game, leaving third-string right guard Hayden Conner as the starting center for Sunday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Andrew Wingard
injuryReports.returnComment: Wingard was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice but ended Week 10 prep with consecutive DNPs. The free safety remains questionable despite multiple absences, but if he is inactive come game time, Kitan Crawford is set to start in his place.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: Fehoko is a 2021 fifth-round pick who turned 29 earlier this month and has been targeted on just two of 37 routes for the Cardinals this year. He mostly seems to have stuck around the league because his size is useful for special teams and blocking, but Fehoko now has a chance to get more snaps on offense, if only because Arizona's WR depth chart has been decimated. He has a chance to start this Sunday against the Rams in QB Carson Beck's first career start.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday against the Rams in what will be the first career start for rookie QB Carson Beck.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.
injuryReports.injury: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Higgins was scheduled for free agency after this season, and he's taken on a larger role as the year has progressed, helping the Cardinals get by with limited talent at wide receiver. Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and won't be of much fantasy interest unless McBride misses time.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins is signing a contract extension with the Cardinals through 2029, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Darius Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Budda Baker
injuryReports.returnComment: The star safety has now logged three 11-tackle games this season, and Baker remains one of the bright spots for a Cardinals team that doesn't have many in 2026. The 10th-year pro was mentioned in trade rumors prior to Tuesday's deadline, but he'll finish out the campaign in Arizona. He's up to 62 tackles (29 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. Baker appears headed for an eighth straight Pro Bowl selection.
injuryReports.injury: Baker recorded 11 tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Max Melton
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Hunter Long
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end was injured in Week 4 against the Giants but had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano have been soaking up the snaps at the position behind Trey McBride in recent weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: Arizona first dealt Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore last Friday, and then Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right elbow during this past Sunday's game at Seattle and will undergo season-ending surgery. That series of events precedes Beck taking over as the Cards' No. 1 signal-caller, and with eight other skill-position players on reserve lists at the moment, the top talents available to the offense will be TE Trey McBride and RB Tyler Allgeier.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Beck will start Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Gardner Minshew II
injuryReports.returnComment: With Minshew already on injured reserve, the surgery confirms he won't return for Arizona this season. Carson Beck is now Arizona's starting QB for Week 11 against the Rams and beyond.
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Evan Hull
injuryReports.returnComment: Ten of Hull's 12 snaps came on special teams, and he wasn't bale to connect with Gardner Minshew on the latter's pass attempt early in the third quarter. Hull has yet to log a carry through three regular-season appearances with the Cardinals. However, he could operate as the team's RB2 behind Tyler Allgeier for Week 10 against the Rams if Bam Knight doesn't clear the league's concussion protocol for that contest.
injuryReports.injury: Hull failed to haul in his lone target during the Cardinals' 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay registered two catches for eight yards on two targets, returned three kickoffs for 64 yards and brought back two punts for 21 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Michael Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Joey Aguilar
injuryReports.returnComment: Arizona has yet to announce a corresponding move, but top quarterback Gardner Minshew could be headed to injured reserve after sustaining a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks that may require season-ending surgery. An undrafted rookie out of Tennessee, Aguilar joins fellow rookie Carson Beck and veteran journeyman Josh Johnson as the healthy options in the Cardinals' quarterback room. Aguilar will likely settle in as the No. 3 option on the depth chart if Minshew is indeed placed on IR.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals signed Aguilar off the Jaguars' practice squad Tuesday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Ryland played just three snaps during the loss, though he managed to convert his only kick, which came from 28 yards and also served as the team's only points in the game. He now has converted 20 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 16 of his 17 extra-point tries across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland made his lone field-goal attempt during Arizona's loss versus the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Josh Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson will head to Arizona in what will mark the 15th different NFL organization that he's been a part of since entering the league as a fifth-round pick in 2008. The 40-year-old is expected to operate as the primary backup option behind rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who is poised to make his first NFL start Week 10 versus the Rams in place of the injured Gardner Minshew (elbow). With Minshew at risk of missing the remainder of the 2026 campaign while he recovers from a torn UCL, Johnson will likely stick around Arizona until the season concludes.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals signed Johnson off the Bengals' practice squad Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Kendal Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's home game. The rookie fourth-rounder has accumulated 61 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Divine Deablo
injuryReports.returnComment: Deablo was cleared to return for Week 9 against the Bengals after missing the Falcons' two prior games due to a forearm injury. He may have aggravated the injury against Cincinnati, and he logged consecutive DNPs to end Week 10 prep. He hasn't been ruled out yet, but assuming Deablo doesn't play, Harold Perkins would be the top candidate to start alongside Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker.
injuryReports.injury: Forearm

injuryReports.name: C.J. Henderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network, Henderson's extension is worth up to $20 million and includes $11 million guaranteed. Henderson has started at outside cornerback in each of his last six outings, and he was moved into the starting lineup after A.J. Terrell landed on injured reserve in late September due to a groin injury. Across eight regular-season games, Henderson has logged 41 tackles (32 solo), nine pass defenses, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Henderson and the Falcons agreed to a two-year contract extension Friday.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: The extension means Thomas -- a third-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2022 NFL Draft -- will be under contract with the Falcons through the 2029 season. The fifth-year pro has stepped into a larger role defensively this year due to the absences of James Pearce (back) and Jalon Walker (knee, IR), the former of whom missed the first eight games of the 2026 campaign while serving a suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Thomas has accumulated 25 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas and the Falcons agreed to a three-year extension worth up to $33 million Friday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Zachariah Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: Branch missed a Week 9 loss to the Bengals and didn't practice this week. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair took on extra snaps in Branch's absence last week. The good news for Branch is that Atlanta has a bye coming up after Sunday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Cameron Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams was placed on IR before Atlanta's regular-season opener with an ankle injury, but he's now finally back to full strength following Week 9. Starting in Week 10, he projects to fill a depth role at tackle behind veteran Jake Matthews and offseason free-agent acquisition Jawaan Taylor.
injuryReports.injury: The Falcons activated Williams (ankle) from injured reserve Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Josh Woods
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: James Pearce Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Gervon Dexter Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Khalil Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Herbert continued to serve a limited role in his first game since being signed to the active roster from the practice squad, as he played just 11 snaps on offense and nine on special teams. With Brian Robinson (hamstring) set to miss at least another three games, Herbert will likely continue to serve as the team's backup running back behind Bijan Robinson.
injuryReports.injury: Herbert carried the ball once for seven yards and caught two of his three targets for two yards during Atlanta's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Olamide Zaccheaus
injuryReports.returnComment: Zaccheaus briefly left Sunday's game and was evaluated for a possible concussion, but the veteran wide receiver was quickly cleared to return. He has only six catches (on 16 targets) for 26 yards through eight regular-season games, and he's caught one pass or zero in seven of those contests. Zaccheaus isn't a key piece in the Falcons' offense, and that's unlikely to change heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs on Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Zaccheaus caught one of three targets for five yards during the Falcons' 34-17 loss to the Bengals on Sunday in Madrid. He also returned one kickoff for 28 yards and returned two punts for minus-three yards.

injuryReports.name: Jahan Dotson
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.
injuryReports.injury: Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Vorhees
injuryReports.returnComment: The move gives the Falcons additional depth at the guard position behind starters Chris Lindstrom and Matthew Bergeron. Vorhees -- a seventh-round selection of the Ravens in the 2023 NFL Draft -- started in all 17 regular-season games in 2025, but he's started in only two of five contests this year. He also missed two games in October while recovering from a foot injury.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens traded Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the Falcons on Tuesday in exchange for Ryan Neuzil, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Michael Penix Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Drake London
injuryReports.returnComment: Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.
injuryReports.injury: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Bijan Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Yasir Abdullah
injuryReports.returnComment: Abdullah was placed on injured reserve Oct. 10 due to a hamstring injury, and after missing the required four games while on the list, he was designated to return Wednesday and then activated Saturday, setting him up for his first game action since Week 4. A rotational role off the edge is likely for Abdullah due to James Pearce (back) making his season debut and all of Cameron Thomas, Za'Darius Smith and Charles Snowden available to the defense.
injuryReports.injury: Abdullah (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game versus the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Beaux Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.
injuryReports.injury: Collins (hip) is listed as active Sunday against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Samson Ebukam
injuryReports.returnComment: Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Rashod Bateman
injuryReports.returnComment: After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.
injuryReports.injury: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation.

injuryReports.name: Lamar Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamilton suffered a hip injury during the Week 9 loss to Jacksonville and didn't finish the contest. Now, after logging a full practice Thursday, he is good to go for Monday's game against the Chargers, assuming he doesn't suffer a setback along the way. Hamilton has appeared in all nine games for Baltimore during the 2026 campaign, accumulating 60 total tackles (43 solo), one interception and four additional passes defended.
injuryReports.injury: Hamilton (hip) practiced in full Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nate Wiggins
injuryReports.returnComment: Wiggins was inactive for the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. However, after logging a full practice session Thursday, it appears he is good to go for Week 10 against the Chargers. The 23-year-old has appeared in eight games this season, garnering 24 total tackles (17 solo) and four passes defensed.
injuryReports.injury: Wiggins (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Hawkins missed the last three games due to a knee injury. While he practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, he likely has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to suit up Monday night against the Chargers. If Hawkins can't play, K'Von Wallace should continue to see more snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Riley Patterson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Ravens signed Harrison Mevis to their practice squad in addition to signing Patterson to the 53-man roster, but the team intends to utilize Patterson as the kicker for Monday's game. Patterson went 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts in five appearances with the Dolphins this season, with a long of just 41 yards. His career-long made field goal of 54 yards came with Miami last season.
injuryReports.injury: Patterson will be the Ravens' kicker for Monday night's game against the Chargers, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Neuzil
injuryReports.returnComment: Neuzil had started at center in each of the Falcons' first nine games of the season, but he's expected to fill a more versatile backup role in Baltimore, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. In addition to center, Neuzil is capable of playing both guard spots, so he'll likely be the top candidate to start if Cam Jurgens, John Simpson or Vega Ioane misses time at any point.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens acquired Neuzil from the Falcons on Tuesday in exchange for guard Andrew Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuryReports.returnComment: Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.
injuryReports.injury: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Malaki Starks
injuryReports.returnComment: Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Starks finished Baltimore's Week 9 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday with four tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Roquan Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith led his team in tackles on a night when Baltimore had a hard time slowing down the Jaguars' offense. Though he's been bothered by knee and foot issues in recent weeks, the veteran linebacker logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Thursday. Smith is well on his way to another triple-digit tackle campaign with 74 stops, including 2.0 sacks, along with an interception and two forced fumbles through nine contests.
injuryReports.injury: Smith finished with eight tackles (two solo) in Thursday's Week 9 loss to Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Matt Hibner
injuryReports.returnComment: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.
injuryReports.injury: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuryReports.returnComment: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.
injuryReports.injury: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cuevas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.
injuryReports.injury: Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Devontez Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.
injuryReports.injury: Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Justice Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.
injuryReports.injury: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Mark Andrews
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.
injuryReports.injury: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Joe Fagnano
injuryReports.returnComment: Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while adding three rushes for 13 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Zay Flowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.
injuryReports.injury: Flowers brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Adisa Isaac
injuryReports.returnComment: Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Alec Anderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson is all set to suit up as the starting left guard for Sunday's game. The Bills have gotten the entire left side of the offensive line back from injury after the team went without Anderson or Dion Dawkins for its Week 9 win over the Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Anderson (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Dion Dawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Dawkins missed the Bills' Week 9 win over the Vikings due to a rib injury. The star left tackle is all set to suit up against the Jets, while right tackle Spencer Brown (ankle) is listed as doubtful for the contest.
injuryReports.injury: Dawkins (ribs) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Spencer Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown overcame a back injury to suit up for the Bills' Week 9 win over the Vikings on Monday. The right tackle picked up an ankle injury during the contest and ended Week 10 prep with consecutive DNPs. If the right tackle does not suit up for Sunday's game, Tylan Grable would be set to return to a starting role against the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Christian Benford
injuryReports.returnComment: Benford injured his wrist during the Bills' Monday night win over the Vikings, though he returned to the contest after sustaining the injury. The cornerback started Week 10 prep with consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's session. Benford will likely suit up for Sunday's contest to start in a secondary that should be bolstered by the trade-deadline acquisition of Amani Hooker.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Tyrell Shavers
injuryReports.returnComment: Shavers was a full participant in all three practices during Week 10 prep, but he would need to be activated from the reserve/PUP list in order to be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Shavers is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he suffered during the Bills' 27-24 win over the Jaguars in the 2025 AFC wild-card round in January.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Amani Hooker
injuryReports.returnComment: Hooker was one of several players who changed teams before Tuesday's trade deadline, with the Titans sending the veteran safety and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Bills in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick. Hooker's addition bolsters a Bills defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (238.8) this season. It's unclear whether he'll start alongside Cole Bishop immediately or operate in a rotational role in the secondary in his Bills debut.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Joe Brady confirmed Friday that Hooker will play Sunday against the Jets, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuryReports.returnComment: Kincaid was a full practice participant Friday after logging limited sessions the previous two days. He should be fine for his usual role against a porous Jets defense.
injuryReports.injury: Kincaid (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Sam Franklin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Terrel Bernard
injuryReports.returnComment: The ball-hawking linebacker picked off Carson Wentz in the third quarter and almost got another pick later in the second half. Bernard has at least one interception in each of the last four regular seasons and has seven total in that span. Across eight games, all starts, this season, Bernard has logged 57 tackles (29 solo), three pass breakups, including the interception, and a fumble recovery on 91 percent of Buffalo's defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Bernard recorded six tackles (two solo) and a pair of pass breakups, including an interception, in Monday night's 23-6 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Greg Gaines
injuryReports.returnComment: Gaines missed the Bills' last two games while recovering from a calf injury, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll return for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Jets. He's accumulated 11 tackles (three solo) and one fumble recovery through six regular-season games, and his return gives the Bills additional depth on the defensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Gaines (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.

injuryReports.name: Keleki Latu
injuryReports.returnComment: Latu gave the Bills the lead late in the first half when he got open in the back of the end zone and caught a pass from Josh Allen. It was not only his first catch of the campaign but also his first NFL touchdown. Latu has worked primarily on special teams this season, and despite his score Monday, he isn't likely to suddenly be a big part of the passing game given the fact that Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes all remain ahead of him on the tight-end depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: Latu caught his lone target for a 25-yard touchdown Monday in a 23-6 win against the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Jackson Hawes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hawes played a season-high 46 snaps on offense and also played eight snaps on special teams. The 25-year-old has now caught a pass in consecutive games after failing to record any receptions across his first six outings of the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Hawes caught his lone target for eight yards during Buffalo's win over the Vikings on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Bass
injuryReports.returnComment: Bass opened Monday's scoring with a 39-yard field goal in the first quarter before converting on kicks from 25 and 52 yards in the second half. All three of his 50-plus yard field goals this season have come over his last two outings, and he's made all 19 of his field-goal attempts and 23 of 25 PAT's through eight regular-season games. Bass's scoring floor is one of the highest in the NFL given the Bills' juggernaut offense led by MVP candidate Josh Allen. They'll hit the road for Week 10 in an AFC East tilt against the Jets on Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Bass connected on all three of his field-goal attempts and made both of his extra-point tries during the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Dawson Knox
injuryReports.returnComment: Knox's targets, catches and yards were all season highs. He also played 58 offensive snaps against Minnesota. With the blitz-happy Vikings defense opposite them, the Buffalo offense went with heavy tight end sets to try and get more blockers on the field. Knox won't be a recommended fantasy target for Sunday's game against the Jets. He has 13 grabs for 79 yards and a touchdown across eight games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Knox caught four passes for 37 yards on five targets in Monday night's 23-6 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Keon Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets.

injuryReports.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson got just one carry while workhorse No. 1 RB James Cook logged a hearty 31 totes. However, Johnson made one big play as a receiver, hauling in a 36-yard reception on a third-down play early in the third quarter to bring Buffalo into Vikings territory. While Johnson has been nearly invisible as a ball carrier this season, he's been effective in a pass-catching role, racking up 210 yards on 17 catches through six games.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson rushed once for one yard and caught both of his targets for 36 yards against the Vikings in a 23-6 victory Monday.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Shakir
injuryReports.returnComment: Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Shakir secured all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Ray Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.
injuryReports.injury: Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: DJ Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran receiver came into the game without an injury designation related to the shoulder issue he's managing, but Moore still put together a modest performance against a tough Vikings defense that kept pressure on Josh Allen throughout the night. Moore has a combined 7-107-1 line on on 12 targets in the two contests he's suited up for since returning from a two-game absence, and he should have a much better chance of downfield success in a Week 10 road matchup against the Jets' vulnerable defense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Moore secured three of five targets for 25 yards and rushed once for 11 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Josh Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen came into the night undoubtedly expecting to have to work for everything he got, and Brian Flores' aggressive defensive unit helped validate that prognosis by sacking the star signal-caller on four occasions. However, Allen was able to navigate the dangers pretty effectively, spreading the ball around to eight different targets overall. He connected with Keleki Latu from 25 yards out late in the first half for his one touchdown pass, and Allen's lone turnover, a first-quarter interception on a deep shot in the Vikings' end zone, didn't lead to any Minnesota points. Allen hasn't eclipsed the 300-yard threshold since Week 1, but he'll take 2,027 passing yards and a 12:6 TD:INT alongside 285 rushing yards into a Week 10 road divisional clash against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Allen completed 21 of 31 passes for 234 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding six carries for 15 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: James Cook III
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook was repeatedly stonewalled through three quarters by a Vikings run defense that had been fairly beatable, but the star running back continued to get opportunities to test Minnesota's defensive front. That approach finally began paying off on an early fourth-quarter marathon scoring drive, one where Cook recorded runs of nine, six and 11 yards before capping off the march with a five-yard scoring rush to extend Buffalo's 13-6 lead. Cook ultimately fell just a carry short of tying his career high, and he eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the fourth time this season. The fifth-year pro's trip to the end zone extended his touchdown streak to seven games as well, and Cook will head into a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Jets just 186 rushing yards short of his fourth straight 1,000-yard campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Mike Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, which cleared him to practice during Week 10 prep. He logged a trio of limited practices, but the doubtful tag indicates that the veteran defensive back will spend at least one more week on IR. If he's not cleared to play in Week 10, then Jackson's next opportunity to play would be Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Will Lee III
injuryReports.returnComment: Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in Week 8, which prevented him from playing in Week 9 against the Broncos. He was a full participant in practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but his reps were limited during Friday's session, which may have been for maintenance reasons. Regardless, Lee's official status for Sunday's NFC South tilt may not be officially known until the Panthers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Mike Jackson (groin, IR) is listed as doubtful, so it's unclear who the Panthers will turn to at outside cornerback opposite Malcolm DeWalt if Lee is unable to play.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Xavier Legette
injuryReports.returnComment: Legette is trending toward a return from injured reserve after the Panthers listed him as a full practice participant all week. They'll need to activate him by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Legette on the active roster for Sunday's NFC South showdown. Legette was Carolina's No. 3 receiver before the injury, often running clear-out routes while Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker dominated the targets. John Metchie and Brycen Tremayne took on more snaps in Legette's absence over the past month-plus.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks remains on injured reserve and isn't likely to be activated by the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline Saturday. He was listed as a full practice participant at the beginning of the week, but coach Dave Canales revealed Friday that there was a reporting error with Brooks and CB Mike Jackson (groin), both of whom should have been listed as limited. Both were then listed as limited Thursday and Friday, with 'doubtful' designations for Sunday's game. Brooks appears on track to return for Week 11 or 12, at which point he could take a few touches away from Chuba Hubbard.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Bobby Okereke
injuryReports.returnComment: Okereke was estimated as a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he remained sidelined for Thursday's full-speed practice. Barring a return to practice Friday, Okereke could be in line for a second consecutive absence Sunday against the Saints after he racked up 49 tackles (31 solo) through his first seven games with the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Devin Lloyd
injuryReports.returnComment: Lloyd played every single defensive snap and co-led the Panthers in tackles with Tyrel Dodson. It was the fifth time this season that Lloyd has logged at least seven combined tackles, and the fifth-year pro is up to 54 stops (32 solo), including 2.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception and a pick-six) across seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Lloyd posted eight tackles (five solo) and one pass defense during the Panthers' 26-21 loss to the Broncos in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Damien Lewis
injuryReports.returnComment: Lewis has missed the Panthers' last two games due to a knee injury, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's NFC South tilt against the Saints. His return gives the Panthers more depth at offensive guard behind starters Robert Hunt and Torricelli Simpkins.
injuryReports.injury: Lewis (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.

injuryReports.name: John Metchie III
injuryReports.returnComment: Both of Metchie's receptions came in the second half -- he brought in a 15-yarder midway through the third quarter and added a 25-yarder near the end of the fourth. The latter catch took the ball down to Denver's nine-yard line and set up a Panthers touchdown, but Carolina ultimately was unable to complete the comeback. Metchie has been consistent but relatively unremarkable this season, logging either two or three receptions in six straight games but not surpassing Sunday's 40 yards in any of those contests.
injuryReports.injury: Metchie caught both of his targets for 40 yards Sunday in a loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Mitchell Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: For the third game in a row, Evans drew exactly two targets and caught both of them Sunday. With that said, he also again trailed in snaps at tight end (31) behind teammates Tommy Tremble (46) and Darren Waller (35), both of whom also drew more targets in Week 9. Evans' role in the Panthers' passing offense isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats going into a Week 10 matchup at New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: Evans caught both of his two targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 26-21 loss versus the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Trevor Etienne
injuryReports.returnComment: Etienne once again saw limited action offensively, playing just seven snaps. The 2025 fourth-round pick was the only running back other than Chuba Hubbard to record a carry and should continue to serve as the team's No. 2 back while Jonathon Brooks remains sidelined due to an abdomen injury.
injuryReports.injury: Etienne carried the ball two times for seven yards and returned one punt for nine yards during Carolina'a loss Sunday to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuryReports.returnComment: Fitzgerald went without a field-goal make for the second time in three weeks, and he pushed his only field-goal attempt of the day wide right from 43 yards in the second quarter. The miss was his first on a field-goal try this year, and the kicker now has gone 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 21 extra-point attempts over eight regular-season contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Fitzgerald missed his only field-goal attempt and went 3-for-3 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Jaycee Horn
injuryReports.returnComment: Horn has had a productive NFL career, amassing 196 total tackles (139 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and 10 interceptions across 56 regular-season games over six seasons. He underwent surgery on his quad back in September. However, until Horn is back on the field or there is a more informative update, he should be considered week-to-week.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders was active for the first time this season. However, he didn't log any offensive snaps and spent all his time on special teams. The 23-year-old has appeared in 30 regular-season games during his career, amassing 62 catches (77 targets) for 532 yards and two touchdowns. Sanders has had a few quality performances throughout his short NFL career, though he likely won't have an opportunity to get involved offensively moving ahead while Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller are in the mix.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders recorded zero targets during Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Coker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Coker caught four of five targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Tommy Tremble
injuryReports.returnComment: The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Tremble caught four of six targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Darren Waller
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuryReports.returnComment: The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and caught four of five targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to Denver.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Young
injuryReports.returnComment: The fourth-year QB tossed TDs in each of the last three quarters, finding Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan, but Young's attempt to engineer a game-winning drive inside the final two minutes ended on a Nik Bonitto strip sack. It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. He added 13 yards on his only carry and lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Torricelli Simpkins III
injuryReports.returnComment: Simpkins didn't suit up in the Week 8 loss to Green Bay due to an ankle injury, though it won't keep him off the field again for Sunday's meeting with the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Simpkins (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Denver, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Corey Bullock
injuryReports.returnComment: Bullock was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. However, after logging full sessions Thursday and Friday, he is good to go for Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Bullock (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game versus Denver, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger has not been cleared to return to practice since suffering a quadriceps injury in Week 7. The reserve strong safety will miss a third consecutive game due to the injury, leaving Russ Yeast and PJ Jules to back up starter Jordan Battle.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas returned to practice Thursday and was a full participant both Thursday and Friday. He should be ready for Week 11, at which point he'll likely take the No. 3 WR job back from Dohnte Meyers.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: DJ Turner II
injuryReports.returnComment: Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Turner (ankle) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Brian Parker II
injuryReports.returnComment: Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jalen Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis was placed on injured reserve in late September after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals now have 21 days to officially activate the 30-year-old for him to remain eligible to play this season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Bryan Cook
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook had his most productive outing of the campaign, logging a season-high 10 tackles. The 2022 second-round pick will look to build on this performance and keep producing during the team's Week 10 matchup versus the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Cook registered 10 tackles (five solo) during the Bengals' win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter had one of his most productive outings of the season during the victory, as he matched Bryan Cook for the most tackles on the team in addition to recording his first interception of the campaign. The 2025 fourth-round pick has racked up 68 tackles (28 solo), including 1.5 sacks, an interception and two forced fumbles across eight games this season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Carter compiled 10 tackles (two solo), an interception and a pass deflection during Cincinnati's win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, Meyers has settled in as the Bengals' third receiver behind target hogs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers would need an injury to one of those two to become relevant again in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught two passes for 47 yards on three targets in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out-produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a modest role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.
injuryReports.injury: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson was able to convert multiple field-goal tries in a game for the first time since Week 3, nailing a 57-yarder in the final moments of the first half before later adding a 43-yard make in the fourth quarter. The kicker had gone back-to-back games without a field-goal attempt, but he has now gone a perfect 12-for-12 on field-goal tries, including 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts while making all four of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Cedric Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday against the Falcons in Madrid.

injuryReports.name: Cashius Howell
injuryReports.returnComment: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Colbie Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Young went without a target while playing 19 of the Bengals' 74 snaps on offense in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Quincy Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams has had his practice reps over the last couple of weeks limited while tending to a hamstring injury, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game, and that trend will continue for Sunday's home tilt. The veteran linebacker has accumulated 62 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and four forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Williams (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Houston.

injuryReports.name: Carson Schwesinger
injuryReports.returnComment: Schwesinger opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices while tending to a wrist injury, but his full session Friday was enough for the second-year linebacker to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Schwesinger's 89 total tackles through nine regular-season games are third-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107) and Nakobe Dean (99).
injuryReports.injury: Schwesinger (wrist) does not have an injury designation against the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: Ward was managing a quad injury during all of Week 10 prep, but he avoided an injury tag for Sunday's game despite not logging a full practice. The veteran defensive back has 34 tackles (19 solo), nine pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Ward (quadriceps) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Michael Burton
injuryReports.returnComment: Burton injured his calf during the Browns' Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints. He was cleared to return in that contest but was unable to practice during Week 10 prep. The Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man active roster nor the practice squad, so they may have to utilize tight end Blake Whiteheart as a backfield blocker. Burton will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Browns' Week 11 bye, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Ronnie Hickman
injuryReports.returnComment: Hickman entered the league's concussion protocol following the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he recorded nine tackles (four solo) and two pass defenses. He was unable to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep, and his absence means rookie second-rounder Emmanuel McNeil-Warren will likely start alongside Grant Delpit at safety, with Daniel Thomas and Donovan McMillon both providing depth at the position. The Browns are on a bye for Week 11, so Hickman will have additional time to progress through the five-step concussion protocol before Week 12 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: After logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday, Fannin's full practice to close the week paves the way for him to continue to lead the Browns' TE corps this weekend. Through nine games thus far, Fannin has yielded fantasy lineup utility by compiling a 37/453/4 receiving line on 53 targets in that span.
injuryReports.injury: Fannin (groin) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Boston
injuryReports.returnComment: With that in mind, coach Todd Monken noted Friday that Boston "moved around pretty good...it's trending in the right way." It's worth noting, however, that Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer relays that Boston left the team's locker room in a walking boot, but it's possible that's simply a precautionary measure. Either way, the wideout's Week 10 status will be known prior to the first batch of games Sunday, with the Browns kicking off at 1:00 pm ET. Assuming he's available this weekend, Boston and fellow rookie KC Concepcion would be in line to lead Cleveland's WR corps versus Houston, with Jerry Jeudy also in the mix.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Myles Harden
injuryReports.returnComment: Harden took down Tyler Shough for 10- and six-yard sacks in the third and fourth quarters, respectively, which were the former's first sacks of his three-year NFL career. The 2024 seventh-rounder is up to 33 tackles (19 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Harden recorded five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Shedeur Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record over their first eight games before developing concussion symptoms and being placed in the NFL's five-step protocol last week. Though Watson cleared protocol last Saturday, his lack of on-field reps during the week prompted the Browns to keep him inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Saints. Sanders stepped in under center and overcame a slow start to finish with 297 passing yards, 28 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns and no turnovers in a 23-22 overtime loss, with his performance drawing praise from head coach Todd Monken. Though the Browns will go back to a healthy Watson for Week 10, Sanders' strong outing in New Orleans could put Watson on shakier ground atop the depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders will return to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Texans after the Browns announced Wednesday that Deshaun Watson (concussion) will draw the Week 10 start, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Deshaun Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol this past Saturday, but because he managed just one limited practice during Week 9 prep, the Browns opted to make him inactive for their matchup with the Saints. Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the season and threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the team's 23-22 overtime loss in New Orleans, but he'll return to the No. 2 role this week while a healthy Watson reclaims the starting job. Though the Browns have gone 5-3 with Watson under center this season, he hasn't been without his flaws (six turnovers, 33 sacks taken). As such, Watson may need a strong showing against the Texans to hold off Sanders for the starting job in the weeks to come.
injuryReports.injury: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Andre Szmyt
injuryReports.returnComment: Szmyt was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the eighth straight game, and his three makes matched a season high for the 28-year-old. The kicker made a 41-yarder in the second quarter and a 30-yard attempt in the third quarter before tying the game up at 16-16 with a 51-yard make with eight seconds left in regulation. Szmyt has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Szmyt went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Jerry Jeudy
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran wideout had zero grabs headed into the Browns' finals drive of regulation, but a 30-yard grab down the left sideline followed up a by a seven-yard gain two plays later set Cleveland up for the game-tying field goal to send it to overtime. The fourth option in the passing attack for the Browns, Jeudy has 18 catches for 208 yards and no touchdowns through nine games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Jeudy caught two of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Sampson
injuryReports.returnComment: Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.
injuryReports.injury: Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards while catching three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss against the Saints.

injuryReports.name: KC Concepcion
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie -- who briefly exited the contest after sustained what appeared to be a right leg issue -- to did the rest by eluding a couple defenders. It was Concepcion's first career NFL touchdown, and he sports a 37-437-1 line on 55 targets through his first nine games for the Browns. If Sanders takes over from Deshaun Watson (concussion) on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays for Concepcion.
injuryReports.injury: Concepcion caught four of six targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added three yards on his only carry.

injuryReports.name: Quinshon Judkins
injuryReports.returnComment: The Browns' running game once again struggled, with the team averaging just 2.8 yards per carry overall, and Judkins' longest gain went for only 12 yards. Dylan Sampson saw a season-high 11 touches to Judkins' 16, and the backfield could be drifting toward a timeshare as coach Todd Monken looks for solutions. Judkins has topped 70 rushing yards in a game just once all season, and he seems unlikely to break out in a Week 10 meeting with the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Judkins carried the ball 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Dillon Gabriel
