Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Lance
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.
injuryReports.injury: Lance failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Smyth
injuryReports.returnComment: Smyth was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 9 overtime win over Cleveland. He served as New Orleans' kicker in the contest and went 3-for-4 on FGAs while making both of his PAT attempts. That performance was likely good enough for Smyth to be elevated again for this Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: The Saints reverted Smyth to their practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Devaughn Vele
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Juwan Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Nahshon Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: A back injury prevented Wright from playing against the Chiefs in Week 9. He logged a full practice Friday, but it wasn't enough for him to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's AFC East tilt. His absence would mean less depth in the Jets' secondary and one less contributor on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Harrison Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: Phillips missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep while recovering from an ankle injury. He was a full participant in Friday's session, so he may be considered more toward the probable side of playing Sunday. If Phillips cannot play, then both Jack Heflin and Payton Page would be in line for more rotational snaps on the interior defensive line behind Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Joseph Ossai
injuryReports.returnComment: Ossai has a chance to return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury after stringing together a trio of limited practices during Week 10 prep. His return would give the Jets additional depth at defensive end behind Kingsley Enagbare and David Bailey.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jarvis Brownlee Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Brownlee was unable to practice Thursday due to an illness, but he was back on the field Friday in a limited capacity. He'll have the weekend to shake off his illness, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Jets announce their list of inactive players. Rookie second-rounder D'Angelo Ponds would have a larger role in the Jets' secondary if Brownlee is not cleared to play.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Trevin Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace was held out of practice all week while recovering from a groin injury, which will prevent him from playing in a second consecutive game. Most of his snaps this season have come on special teams, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at linebacker for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Wallace's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The same goes for top receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) as well as Adonai Mitchell (knee). The trio's full practice participation Friday suggests that all three players will be available Sunday, but their statuses will nonetheless need to be confirmed ahead of Week 10 action due to their official game designations. Fortunately for fantasy managers who have shares in any of the Jets' top three WRs, the team kicks off at 1:00 pm ET on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Adonai Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Fellow wideouts Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper (ankle) also are listed as questionable despite being full practice participants Friday. Both figure to play, as does Mitchell, who finished without a catch on seven targets (two drops) in last week's loss to the Chiefs -- one week after catching seven passes for 142 yards and a TD against the Raiders. Wilson's likely return to the lineup means Mitchell isn't assured of similar volume moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Garrett Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson will upgrade to full participation Friday after logging limited practices earlier in the week. He's on track to return after missing just one game, but he'll still need clearance from a neurologist if Friday's practice goes as planned.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: David Bailey
injuryReports.returnComment: Bailey had a productive outing despite the loss as he was the only Jets defender to record a sack. The 23-year-old has gotten off to a strong start during his rookie campaign, compiling 34 tackles (26 solo), including 7.5 sacks, and five forced fumbles across his first eight games.
injuryReports.injury: Bailey tallied nine tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two forced fumbles during the Jets' loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.
injuryReports.injury: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.

injuryReports.name: Mason Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Troy Reeder
injuryReports.returnComment: Reeder is returning to New York after having been released by the Jets in October. The 32-year-old has logged four tackles (one solo) across six outings this season and will likely continue to see the majority of his playing time come on special teams during his second tenure with the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: The Jets signed Reeder to their active roster Monday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Will McDonald IV
injuryReports.returnComment: The 2023 first-round pick racked up 18.5 sacks over the previous two seasons and has three on his ledger through nine games in 2026, but he's seen his playing time tail off with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick David Bailey and the addition of Kingsley Enagbare in free agency. Though McDonald is hopeful to land with a team that can present him with a clearer path to a full-time role, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that McDonald "is going to be here" once the deadline passes, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.
injuryReports.injury: McDonald put in a request for the Jets to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Ian Rapoport and Rich Cimini of ESPN report.

injuryReports.name: Jason Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders provided all the offense for New York in Week 9, making exactly four field goals for the second straight week and third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards before pulling his lone miss wide left from 53 yards, all of which came in the first half. Sanders has now gone 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Kenyon Sadiq
injuryReports.returnComment: After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.
injuryReports.injury: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Geno Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards.

injuryReports.name: Braelon Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Breece Hall
injuryReports.returnComment: Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.
injuryReports.injury: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: VJ Payne
injuryReports.returnComment: Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Dane Belton
injuryReports.returnComment: Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Belton recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo) and a pass defensed in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jamien Sherwood
injuryReports.returnComment: Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Sherwood recorded 14 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Harmon
injuryReports.returnComment: Harmon missed the Steelers' four games prior to the Week 9 bye while on injured reserve due to a foot injury. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and ended Week 10 prep with a full session Friday, but he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown. Harmon's return would bolster the Steelers' defensive line behind Yahya Black, Keeanu Benton and Cameron Heyward.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: DeShon Elliott
injuryReports.returnComment: Elliott had no injury designation in practice Thursday after popping up as a limited participant in practice Wednesday. The 29-year-old has played just two games through nine weeks of the NFL regular season. He returned from injured reserve in Week 7, totaling two tackles (two solo) on the season.
injuryReports.injury: Elliott was a full participant in practice Thursday, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Brandin Echols
injuryReports.returnComment: Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Echols (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Doneiko Slaughter
injuryReports.returnComment: Slaughter was unable to play against the Browns in Week 8 due to a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing. His ability to log a full session Wednesday puts him on track to play against the Bengals on Sunday, when he's expected to play mostly on special teams while providing the Steelers depth in the secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Slaughter (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Ben Skowronek
injuryReports.returnComment: Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Skowronek (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Chris Boswell
injuryReports.returnComment: Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Boswell made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Germie Bernard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Pat Freiermuth
injuryReports.returnComment: With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.
injuryReports.injury: Freiermuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. He added one rushing attempt for a one-yard touchdown.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns.

injuryReports.name: Rico Dowdle
injuryReports.returnComment: Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: DK Metcalf
injuryReports.returnComment: Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Rodgers
injuryReports.returnComment: Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Rodgers completed 13 of 25 passes for 172 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Warren
injuryReports.returnComment: Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: The Steelers signed Smith off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Trent Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams downgraded to a non-participant in Friday's practice after upgrading to a limited participant for Thursday's session. The left tackle was likely taking vet rest ahead of Sunday's game as he prepares to suit up through his shoulder injury against the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Renardo Green
injuryReports.returnComment: Green missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep due to a back injury that he sustained during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9. He was limited in Friday's practice, and if he cannot play Sunday, then rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock and Nate Hobbs (groin, IR) would be candidates for elevated roles in the secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Deommodore Lenoir
injuryReports.returnComment: Lenoir injured his foot during the 49ers' Week 9 win over the Raiders. He was able to log a limited practice Friday after being sidelined both Wednesday and Thursday, and that limited session was enough for him to draw the questionable tag. Rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock and Ashtyn Davis would be in line for more snaps in the secondary if Lenoir is unable to play Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Dre Greenlaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Greenlaw tweaked his knee during Thursday's practice, but he was cleared to participate in Friday's session in a limited capacity, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com. Garret Wallow, Tatum Bethune and Luke Gifford would all be in line to start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger if Greenlaw is unable to play Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Samuel was back on the practice field this week for the first time since injuring his right hamstring in Week 5 at Seattle, turning in limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. It was enough to get the clear to return to action this weekend. With Mike Evans (Achilles) out again, Samuel likely will be among the top WRs at the disposal of QB Brock Purdy along with newcomer Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins.
injuryReports.injury: Samuel (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Mike Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: Evans thus will miss his third game in a row due to the right Achilles injury that he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning to action and likely would play this weekend if it was a playoff matchup. Instead, the 49ers will continue to exercise caution with their No. 1 WR. With Evans again sidelined Sunday, Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing represent the options at the position available to QB Brock Purdy.
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Keenan Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen could have a significant role immediately, joining an injury-riddled WR room, though Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been cleared to play this Sunday. Mike Evans (Achilles) is out again, leaving Samuel, Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins as the top healthy options at wide receiver. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan mentioned Wednesday that Allen still has some risk of being suspended at some point this season due to an August arrest for DUI while he was with the Colts, per 95.7 The Game.
injuryReports.injury: Allen will play for the 49ers in Sunday's game at Dallas after being acquired in a trade earlier this week, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Jaden Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger set the tone for the 49ers right out of halftime, when he intercepted a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tre Tucker and returned it 35 yards for a pick-six for the first defensive touchdown of Dugger's young NFL career. The rookie fifth-rounder has logged at least six solo tackles in three of his last four games and is up to 36 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pick-six through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Dugger recorded six solo tackles and a pick-six during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Fred Warner
injuryReports.returnComment: Warner's five stops tied a season low, although he did recover the fumble late in the third quarter that the 49ers' offense converted into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Jordan Watkins seven plays later. Warner has played every single defensive snap in each of the 49ers' last six games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 77 tackles (36 solo), including 0.5 sacks, three pass defenses, five forced fumbles and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Warner logged five tackles (three solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: C.J. West
injuryReports.returnComment: The 49ers opened West's 21-day practice window Wednesday, and he was limited in his return to on-field practice. He landed on injured reserve in late September due to a knee injury, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Upton Stout
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Gracen Halton
injuryReports.returnComment: Halton suffered a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over Las Vegas and is out for the season. The fourth-round rookie finished his inaugural NFL campaign with 15 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, a defensed pass, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery (which he returned for a touchdown) over eight contests. San Francisco's recent acquisition of DeForest Buckner softens the blow of losing Halton a bit.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brandin Cooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense figures to decrease with Keenan Allen now in the fold, and with Evans or Samuel potentially ready to return.
injuryReports.injury: Cooks brought in both of his targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Demarcus Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson caught three passes for 22 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Mac Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries for Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.

injuryReports.name: Jordan James
injuryReports.returnComment: As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.
injuryReports.injury: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Eddy Pineiro
injuryReports.returnComment: Pineiro continues to see the majority of his action handling extra-point duties, as he's now attempted just two field goals across his last three outings and only 10 total on the season. Sunday's performance also marked just the second time this season that the 31-year-old didn't miss a kick.
injuryReports.injury: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and all five of his extra-point tries during San Francisco's win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aiyuk
injuryReports.returnComment: In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.
injuryReports.injury: Personal

injuryReports.name: Kaelon Black
injuryReports.returnComment: Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Black rushed 11 times for 70 yards but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Watkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.
injuryReports.injury: Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Quenton Nelson
injuryReports.returnComment: Nelson's absence doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he underwent a minor procedure on his injured knee Monday. He's currently considered week-to-week, and with the Seahawks on a bye for Week 11, Nelson could return for Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Grey Zabel will likely start at left guard Sunday in Nelson's stead.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Charles Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: Cross logged a limited practice Thursday before being held out of Friday's session, and he'll end up missing a third consecutive game due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered against the Chiefs in Week 7. The Seahawks are on bye for Week 11, so Cross will extra time to recover before Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Josh Jones will likely start at left tackle in Cross's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brandon Pili
injuryReports.returnComment: Pili missed the Seahawks' last two games while nursing a back injury, but he's been cleared to play in Week 10 after logging a full practice session Friday. His return gives the Seahawks more depth on the interior defensive line behind Byron Murphy.
injuryReports.injury: Pili (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Uchenna Nwosu
injuryReports.returnComment: Nwosu has missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to an ankle injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after ending Week 10 prep with a full practice Friday. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and Connor O'Toole.
injuryReports.injury: Nwosu (ankle) does not have an injury designation against the Raiders on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Derick Hall
injuryReports.returnComment: Hall was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 10 prep before sitting out Friday's session. However, his reduced practice reps appear to have been planned by the Seahawks to manage his back injury, and the fourth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. Hall has 24 tackles (14 solo), including 3.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Hall (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Leonard Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a shoulder injury, which prevented him from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Mike Morris and Rylie Mills will operate in expanded roles on defense in the absence of Williams, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29, since the Seahawks are on a bye for Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Drew Lock
injuryReports.returnComment: Lock was listed as limited on the Seahawks' first two Week 10 injury reports due to a lingering right elbow issue and a new oblique concern. He spoke of the latter injury Thursday, telling Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle that he's "feeling good," and Lock's ability to avoid a designation confirms as much ahead of Sunday's matchup. In three appearances (two starts) this season, Lock has completed 54 of 76 passes (71 percent) for 597 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions.
injuryReports.injury: Lock (right elbow/oblique) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Brady Henderson of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Ernest Jones IV
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones finished tied for second on the team in tackles behind Julian Love during Sunday's victory. Jones has now racked up seven or more tackles in all nine of his outings to start the season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: Jones tallied seven tackles (three solo) during Seattle's win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Rashid Shaheed
injuryReports.returnComment: Shaheed suffered a knee injury during a Week 7 win against the Chiefs and missed the last two games as a result. Now that he's unhindered on the practice field, though, he'll resume his standing as Seattle's No. 2 WR and primary kick and punt returner
injuryReports.injury: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Emanuel Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Cooper Kupp
injuryReports.returnComment: All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: George Holani
injuryReports.returnComment: Holani logged just two offensive snaps, by far his lowest count in a game of the season. He's trending toward playing primarily on special teams now that Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back in the fold at running back for Seattle. Emanuel Wilson also is on the roster, but he didn't see any action at all in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Holani didn't log any touches or targets Sunday in a 17-3 win over Arizona.

injuryReports.name: Tory Horton
injuryReports.returnComment: Horton has just seven catches for 67 yards across six games since Week 3. The Seahawks' No. 3 receiver is well off the fantasy radar, even with Rashid Shaheed (knee) injured.
injuryReports.injury: Horton caught two passes for 22 yards on three targets in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Jason Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: The Seahawks' offense put forth a relatively modest showing in Week 9 with backup quarterback Drew Lock (oblique) at the helm, but Myers made good on the few opportunities that he did have, rebounding somewhat from a rough game in Week 8 where he missed two kicks. Starting quarterback Sam Darnold (quadriceps) will again be out in Week 10 at Las Vegas, but Myers will at least have the benefit of kicking indoors come Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Myers made his only field-goal attempt and converted both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Sam Darnold
injuryReports.returnComment: Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Jadarian Price
injuryReports.returnComment: Price received one more touch than Week 8's 12 but more than doubled his yards from scrimmage from 37 to 78. Having said that, backfield mate Zach Charbonnet went from nine touches last Monday against the Bears to 17 in Week 9 while pacing the Seahawks in total yards with 86. Price and Charbonnet appear poised to split the RB reps moving forward, but the former may be the change-of-pace option while the latter handles early downs.
injuryReports.injury: Price posted nine carries for 24 yards and secured all four targets for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 victory versus the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Zach Charbonnet
injuryReports.returnComment: The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.
injuryReports.injury: Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: AJ Barner
injuryReports.returnComment: Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.
injuryReports.injury: Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown.

injuryReports.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith-Njigba was working with backup QB Drew Lock for the third time this season, as the latter was filling in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib). The result was a season low in receiving yards, which was only the second time this season in which Smith-Njigba failed to reach the century mark. Despite the subpar outing for him, he surpassed 1,000 yards on the campaign for a third straight season, with eight games still to go. Darnold may also be sidelined next Sunday at Las Vegas, which again could impact Smith-Njigba's chances to produce as he has most weeks in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Smith-Njigba reeled in seven of 10 targets for 51 yards during Sunday's 17-3 win against the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Milroe
injuryReports.returnComment: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.
injuryReports.injury: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyrice Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight opened Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices before logging a full session Saturday, and he's done enough to fade an injury tag against Chicago. The third-year linebacker has seen an uptick in defensive snaps over his last two outings, and he's logged 16 tackles (nine solo) in that span.
injuryReports.injury: Knight (hip) doesn't have an injury designation for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Tommy Townsend
injuryReports.returnComment: Townsend didn't play in Week 8 due to a knee injury that he sustained in Week 7 against the Browns. He had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 9 bye and was a full practice participant Wednesday and Thursday. However, Townsend was held out of Friday's session, and a right Achilles injury was added to his designation. Thomas Morstead will likely be called up from the practice squad to punt for the Titans on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Peter Skoronski
injuryReports.returnComment: Skoronski injured his hamstring against the Bengals in Week 8, and the Week 9 bye did not provide enough recovery time to return for Week 10. Garrett Dellinger filled in at left guard following Skoronski's injury, although head coach Robert Saleh told reporters Friday that he has not committed to a starting LG for Sunday's AFC South tilt. Skoronski's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Cody Barton
injuryReports.returnComment: Barton was unable to practice during Week 10 prep while in the league's concussion protocol, which he may have entered following the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. Rookie second-rounder Anthony Hill (neck) has also been ruled out, which leaves Dorian Mausi and Mohamoud Diabate as the likely candidates to start at linebacker alongside Cedric Gray for Sunday's contest. Barton's next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22, although he would have to return to practice in at least a limited capacity to demonstrate that he's progressing in the league's five-step protocol.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Anthony Hill Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill may have injured his neck during the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. The Week 9 bye provided the rookie second-rounder extra time to rest, but he was not cleared to practice during Week 10 prep and will miss his first game of the regular season. Cody Barton (concussion) has also been ruled out, so Mohamoud Diabate and Dorian Mausi both figure to start alongside Cedric Gray at linebacker for Sunday's AFC South tilt. Hill's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Chimere Dike
injuryReports.returnComment: Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again this Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Dike may have a significant role on offense with Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Tony Pollard
injuryReports.returnComment: Pollard sat out Thursday's session with a listed combo of 'finger/rest,' but given that he worked fully Friday, it was likely more of a maintenance day for Tennessee's clear-cut top back. In that role, Pollard has made his mark from a fantasy perspective by averaging 16.6 carries for 74.4 yards, with 14 catches for 70 yards and six rushing scores in eight games to date.
injuryReports.injury: Pollard (finger/rest) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyjae Spears
injuryReports.returnComment: A return to action after missing two games would hurt Tony Pollard's workload projection, though Pollard would still be in line for most of the carries. There have also been hints of rookie Nicholas Singleton getting playing time in the second half of the season, leaving Spears without much of a path to mainstream fantasy value.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Carnell Tate
injuryReports.returnComment: There was previously some optimism that Tate -- who last played in Week 7 -- would be able to return after the Titans' Week 9 bye, but the wideout's absence will continue at least until Nov. 22 against the Cowboys, a contest that coach Robert Saleh is hopeful the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL draft will be back for, per Turron Davenport of ESPN.com. For now, added WR snaps/targets will be available for Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor alongside Wan'Dale Robinson, with Calvin Ridley also mixing in, an arrangement that was in play during Tennessee's Nov. 1 loss to the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: JC Latham
injuryReports.returnComment: Latham injured his finger in the fourth quarter of the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. He had extra time to rest thanks to the Week 9 bye, and given his full participation in Wednesday's practice, Latham should suit up as the Titans' starting left guard for Sunday's AFC South showdown against the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Latham (finger) practiced in full Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jaylon Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones was unable to play in the Titans' Week 8 loss to the Bengals due to a knee injury. He had extra time to recover courtesy of the Week 9 bye, and the fourth-year defensive back's full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available to play against the Jaguars on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Marcus Harris
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year cornerback was injured in the Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals, but the bye came at the right time, and he appears to be ready to go for Sunday's date with the Jaguars. Harris has functioned as Tennessee's slot corner this season, so he figures to see plenty of Parker Washington in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Harris (ankle) practiced in full Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: James Williams Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: In a corresponding transaction, Tennessee activated linebacker Dorian Mausi from injured reserve. Williams won't be able to return to game action until Week 14 against the Lions at the earliest. In the meantime, Mausi figures to assume the small role Williams was occupying.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Dorian Mausi
injuryReports.returnComment: Mausi has been on IR since late August with a foot injury, but it now looks like he'll finally be ready to return to game action in Week 10. In 17 regular-season games with Tennessee in 2025, all 341 of his snaps came on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: The Titans activated Mausi (foot) from injured reserve Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Nicholas Singleton
injuryReports.returnComment: A fifth-round pick out of Penn State, Singleton was a healthy inactive for four of the Titans' first eight games prior to a Week 9 bye and has logged more snaps on special teams than offense thus far during his rookie season. However, with the 29-year-old Pollard set to become a free agent after the season and likely not part of the 1-7 Titans' rebuilding effort, playing time could become up for grabs in the backfield if Tennessee receives an appealing trade offer for the veteran. Along with Singleton, Tyjae Spears (knee) and Michael Carter would be vying for reps in the event Pollard is traded, while Julius Chestnut is another option in the backfield but has been utilized almost exclusively on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that Singleton is "getting better," and the rookie running back could be a candidate to see added opportunities in the second half of the season if lead back Tony Pollard is dealt ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Calvin Ridley
injuryReports.returnComment: Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.
injuryReports.injury: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Joey Slye
injuryReports.returnComment: The kicker drilled field goals from 46 and 29 yards out. Slye has only missed one kick this year, a field goal, but the Titans' offense has not been consistent enough to give him ample opportunities on a weekly basis.
injuryReports.injury: Slye hit both field-goal tries and his two extra-point attempts in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Elic Ayomanor
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Ayomanor's role didn't grow much, as Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm and Chimere Dike combined to see 22 of the team's 39 targets. Through eight games this season, Ayomanor has 13 grabs for 211 yards and a touchdown on 26 targets.
injuryReports.injury: Ayomanor caught three of five targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Gunnar Helm
injuryReports.returnComment: Helm led the team in targets while he was able to register a new career-high 76 receiving yards in the contest. The tight end has now reeled in eight passes over the last two weeks after he caught nine of 13 targets for 60 yards over the first six games of the 2026 campaign. Helm will have a tough test against the Jaguars in Week 10 after the team's bye week in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Helm caught five of nine targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Robinson didn't experience a significant change in role in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder), as this was the fourth consecutive game in which Robinson notched either six or seven targets. His 57 receiving yards tied a season high, and Robinson scored his third touchdown of the season on a 15-yard catch in the fourth quarter. The Titans took a seven-point lead with 3:46 remaining after a successful two-point conversion following Robinson's TD, but the Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown drive and eventually won in OT to drop the Titans to 1-7. Robinson and the Titans will be on bye in Week 9 before returning to action against the Jaguars in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson caught six of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Cam Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion.

injuryReports.name: John Franklin-Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: Franklin-Myers drew the questionable tag after ending Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices, and the veteran defensive lineman has been cleared by medical staff to suit up Sunday. He has 14 tackles (six solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through seven regular-season games, but he'll be tasked with a larger role on the defensive line in the absence of Jeffery Simmons, the latter of whom was traded to the Bears on Thursday.
injuryReports.injury: Franklin-Myers (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

sources.name: Devin Duvernay
sources.returnComment: A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.

sources.returnComment: Jefferson averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

00-0040676.injury: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion.

sources.name: Cam Ward
sources.returnComment: Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

sources.name: Devin Duvernay
sources.returnComment: A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.

The Titans took a seven-point lead with 3:46 remaining after a successful two-point conversion following Robinson's TD, but the Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown drive and eventually won in OT to drop the Titans to 1-7. Robinson and the Titans will be on bye in Week 9 before returning to action against the Jaguars in Week 10.
sources.injury: Robinson caught six of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He also lost a fumble.

health.injury: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.

sources.name: Calvin Ridley
sources.returnComment: Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.

sources.returnComment: Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again this Sunday.

qbChemistry.method: Starter-linked weekly statistics; starting QB must supply at least 80% of team attempts and 15 attempts. Two-year recency half-life, eight-game pair and five-game comparison shrinkage; maximum 15% receiving change. Target allocation is conserved within each forecast team. No unsupported same-QB sample means no chemistry adjustment.
limitations: Starter-linked team-game splits are observational, not exact passer-target charting.
Role, opponent and scheme differences can confound historical splits.
Not yet validated out of sample; adjusted markets cannot pass the betting quality gate.

workloadContext.methodology: Conditional expected-lineup research allocation, not a validated improvement to the forest. No arbitrary play probability for questionable returns. Historical coappearance is descriptive, not proof of causal injury effects. Missing player rows are not zero-filled as game outcomes.
workloadContext.scope: Current-team QB/RB/WR/TE opportunities. Archived actual statistics and sportsbook quotes are never rewritten.

tdReport.orderMethodology: First and last TD fair odds come from separate player-game models trained on actual first/last scorer IDs, including defensive/return TDs in the event order and overtime. They use lagged opportunity and prior scoring-order rates; ATTD probabilities are not reused as first/last estimates. Game-level probability caps reserve mass for unmodeled scorers and no-TD outcomes. Book settlement rules may differ.
